decks.title: Your website: a guided tour
decks.desc: What is on the new site, the five designs, English and Hebrew, and what happens next.

slides.sub: Private Hebrew Tuition with Lee-Elle Horowitz

points: Every word comes from the text you supplied, and a few facts from your Spotlight profile.
Nothing is invented: no prices, no pupils, no reviews, no qualifications you did not give.
No contact details are shown until you choose them.
Every page says Draft until you approve it.

slides.h: Five designs, each built around its own idea

slides.p: The home page for now. A large Hebrew letter opens each section, the whole alphabet runs across the page, and your nine kinds of lesson are letter tiles.
The page as a chat: the questions a parent asks, and your answers, one by one.
Past, present and future, the way you teach grammar: your story, lessons today, and where a student wants to get to.
From your acting training: a theatre programme, with Hebrew as the main act and music in the second half.
A ruled exercise book: one plain column, for a parent who wants the facts, and it prints cleanly.

slides.h: Every design, in English and in Hebrew
slides.p: The English / עברית switch sits at the top of every page, with a button that stays in the corner. The Hebrew pages read right to left. The Hebrew is a translation of your text, marked as not yet checked by you.
Most parents arrive on a phone. Every page fits a phone screen, works in light and dark mode, and passes the accessibility checks.

points: Which design you like best, or which parts of which.
Corrections to the Hebrew, and your name in Hebrew if you want it.
Your own photos, with the photographer's name for each.
Which contact details, if any, visitors should see; prices and availability only if you want them shown.
Your approval, when you are happy.
For now, send them to Dinis.
A form on the site, for changes, photos and visitors' enquiries, is on its way.
Later, your own Claude can make changes for you, following the rules this site keeps.

slides.h: Plain files, in a place you own
slides.p: No server, no cookies, no tracking. The files, the history and the address can move anywhere, at any time.

decks.title: Behind the scenes: how this site was made
decks.desc: The agents, the pipeline, content in JSON, the checks, the design rounds and what makes the site sovereign.

slides.note: Built on 25 November 2026 by a team of AI agents working for Dinis Cruz

slides.h: One request, a team of agents
steps: takes the request and starts a keeper
creates the repository and the address
b.site.lee-elle-horowitz builds and keeps the site
reviews each round with synthetic parents
lists the site once she approves it
filed in the Sovereign Website factory
seeded with checks and a deploy workflow
the keeper signs every commit with its own key
a push to dev publishes in a minute or two

points: site/data/content/en.json: her words, as she supplied them.
site/data/content/he.json: the Hebrew translation, for her to check.
site.json, start.json, tour.json and admin.json: everything else.
tools/designs/build.py turns them into plain HTML pages, in both languages. It holds no words of its own.
slides.code: en.json + he.json  →  build.py  →  10 design pages, 2 home pages, 2 pickers

points: Build, link previews and internal links.
HTML validity, and accessibility (axe) on every page, in light and in dark mode.
No em dashes, no family strip, a leak scan for secrets.
No page longer than 8,000 px on a phone, and no sideways scrolling.
Nothing loaded from another website: no fonts, scripts or trackers.
design.b's brief asked for five designs, each from its own idea, not colour skins of one layout.
design.b.rounds asked synthetic parents: would you book a Hebrew lesson for your child here?
Round 1 put Hebrew letters in every design, the facts parents look for higher up, and a light version of The stage.
Round 2 fixed the alphabet direction, removed empty placeholders and gave the site one voice: hers.
Each agent makes its own signing key; only the public half is published.
Every commit is signed and carries the agent's name and session.
The keeper's notes, open work and decisions are in the repository, for anyone to read.

slides.p: Static files in one repository: no server code, no cookies, no tracking. It belongs to Lee-Elle, and can move anywhere.
